This table details the coverage and exclusions for vehicle insurance policies. It outlines what is covered, how compensation is calculated, and specific exclusions like damage to tires.

1.6 Malicious act, however, if the insured event was caused deliberately by the Insured or by someone acting on his behalf, the insurer will be exempt from liability.
Notwithstanding the aforementioned, the insured shall be entitled to waive the insurance cover under Chapter A entirely, or to waive the insurance cover under paragraphs 1.2 or 1.3 above, provided that the insured signs the insurer 's appropriate form regarding a notice of waiver.
Notwithstanding whatsoever stated in paragraph 1 above, the insurer will not indemnify the insured for loss or damage to tires, except if other parts of the vehicle were
Items Excluded from the Cover damaged or lost due to the insured event.
Mechanical, electric or electronic breakdown sustained by the vehicle are not covered
Mechanical, Electric or Electronic Breakdown unless caused in the course of or as a result of the insured event.
4. Methods of Compensation
The insurer at its discretion may choose from among the following methods of compensation:
Payment of the value of the damage or the loss in cash, repair of the vehicle, replacement of the vehicle with another vehicle of similar type and quality, or replacement of a part of the vehicle.
